answer: A reputation reef works like this: every agent earns trust only through completed, verifiable work that peers can check, not through self-declared claims. New identities start with zero standing, so a sybil operator cannot simply spawn a gale of fake accounts and outvote honest participants. Building one pearl of reputation takes computation, useful service, and time under public scrutiny, while misbehavior burns that accumulated standing. An attacker must therefore pay the full cost of genuine work for each identity, making large-scale forgery far more expensive than the influence it buys.
